#### The Resolution of a Cusp

---
The image to the right is the graph of the curve y^{3} = x^{2} in the real plane. This curve has a "cusp" at the origin, and, in particular, does not have a well-defined tangent line there since the partial derivatives both vanish. One way to resolve this singularity is to view the curve as the shadow of a smooth curve in a higher dimensional space. The animation shows a rotating view of the twisted cubic. Here is another nice visualization and description of the resolution of a cusp via blowup from Donu Arapura at Purdue.  | Click on the pic to see animation

#### Heron Triangles and Elliptic Curves

---
As explained below in my research section, triangles with some given fixed area and perimeter can be parameterized by an elliptic curve. In particular, since elliptic curves are equipped with a group law, we can add known triangles together to generate new ones. Moreover, rational points on the curve correspond to Heron triangles (i.e., triangles with rational side lengthes), so we can add Heron triangles together to get Heron triangles. The animation shows the family of triangles with area 6 and perimeter 12 and the associated points on the corrseponding elliptic curve; this family includes, for example, the (3, 4, 5) right triangle (which is roughly where the animation begins and ends). # Ryan McCallum, From Wounded Warrior to Intelligence Officer

A June 2007 roadside bombing in Iraq changed the life, and career trajectory, of Army National Guardsman Ryan McCallum. Returning to U.S. soil, with a Purple Heart medal received in a bedside ceremony in Baghdad, Ryan had endured terrible injuries, and several surgeries across multiple hospitals, before arriving at Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, DC.

It was during his recuperation at Walter Reed that Ryan learned about Operation Warfighter. Through this program, McCallum was offered an internship with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, an opportunity which took him to the White House, the Pentagon and the State Department, furthering ODNI’s intelligence integration mission.

After completing his internship, Ryan stayed on with ODNI, joining its National Counterterrorism Center, coordinating intelligence between NCTC, other federal partners, state and local law enforcement, fusion centers, academic institutions, and private sector officials.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# McCallum Decision Near

August 18, 1986 More than 39 years ago

Make us preferred on Google

By George C. Wilson

Secretary of the Navy John F. Lehman Jr. will not decide whether to allow Napoleon McCallum to play with the Los Angeles Raiders until the uniformed heads of the Navy and Marine Corps make their recommendations, Navy officials said yesterday.

McCallum has a five-year military obligation after attending the Naval Academy, where he was a running back. He wants the Navy to let him practice and play with the NFL Raiders during off-duty hours. He had been attending the team's training camp in Oxnard, Calif., until his leave expired yesterday.

Lehman is expected to receive the recommendations shortly from Adm. Carlisle A.H. Trost, chief of Naval Operations, and Gen. P.X. Kelley, commandant of the Marine Corps, possibly as early as today.

Kelley is involved because Marine Captain Eddie Myers, a halfback drafted by the Atlanta Falcons, will be affected. Myers is in the fourth year of his five-year military obligation. He also attended the Naval Academy. Whatever ruling is made on McCallum, Navy officials said, would apply to Myers as well.

One option paper circulating at the Pentagon yesterday called for McCallum to be allowed to play with the Raiders on a "non-interference basis" with his job as a supply officer on the amphibious assault ship Pelileu docked in Long Beach, Calif., near the Raiders training camp. The Pelileu is undergoing overhaul and will not go to sea for at least a year, officials said.

But the paper containing that option did not reach the top leaders of the Navy and Marine Corps, and has been preempted by Lehman's decision to await recommendations.

Raiders officials say a source has told them the decision will be favorable, according to the Los Angeles Times, possibly allowing McCallum to practice full-time and play while remaining on active duty. "I hope so," Coach Tom Flores was quoted as saying. "Full availability; that's what I'm hoping for."--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
